comparison: The reviewed 47.4.3 loader path uses the same file/path checks and platform DEX element construction operations as the previously reviewed 47.5.3 path; obfuscated class names differ.

findings.finding: Builds libdex_<module>.so paths; selects existing files; makes them read-only; passes them to LJII. No archive content digest or fixed size check.
Uses preloaded elements or calls LX/02nX.LIZ, then appends returned elements to DexPathList.dexElements.

Reflectively invokes makePathElements or makeDexElements with the file list and optimized directory. No module checksum argument. The legacy makeDexElements fallback uses the existing generic reflection interceptor; no module-specific digest was found.
Recovery sanity check only tests isFile, length >=4, then first two bytes 0x50 0x4b (PK).

path-elements-v23.txt stores the optimized directory and file absolute paths. readStoredDexPaths checks path existence; sameFile/sameFiles compare paths. No content digest, length, modification time, signature or CRC pin in this class.

Metadata fields are module/project/package/probe class/representative SO/provider projects/service keys. Verification uses Class.forName(probe), BaseDexClassLoader.findLibrary(representative SO) and File.exists. No size or digest fields.
Lists df_ship, df_live_cast and df_pitaya among the libdex modules passed to this loader.

MD5/SHA1/SHA256 of all six original module ZIPs and their eight DEX entries searched as raw digest, ASCII hex and base64 (63 unique patterns; corresponding ABI payloads identical). All 26,616 decompressed entries checked. The only six matches are ordinary parent-APK v1 SHA256 digests in META-INF/MANIFEST.MF. No matching external content digest elsewhere.

conclusion: No external original-content or fixed-size pin found in the reviewed bundled-module loader path. The existing format-aware DEX/ZIP rebuild remains supported by this native evidence when ZIP names, metadata/alignment, CRC, DEX format/checksums/string ordering and all non-target semantics are validated. The changed ship DEX split is handled by per-entry parsing, not a fixed class count.
limits: Static original-APK review; no physical Android execution.
Does not prove absence of every obfuscated/native or remotely supplied integrity policy.
Downloaded splits and unknown modules/builds are outside this conclusion.
The parent APK must be re-signed; original APK v1 digest entries are not retained as valid signatures.
